body.stem: You administer a Microsoft Entra workforce tenant for Contoso. The compliance team has directed that only people holding the Guest Inviter or User Administrator directory role may issue new B2B collaboration invitations. Regular member users and existing guests must lose the ability to invite anyone new. You need to apply the least-privilege change that meets this requirement. Which configuration should you select?

exhibit.text:
External collaboration settings > Guest invite settings

  ( ) Anyone in the organization can invite guest users including guests and non-admins (most inclusive)

  ( ) Member users and users assigned to specific admin roles can invite guest users including guests with member permissions

  ( ) Only users assigned to specific admin roles can invite guest users

  ( ) No one in the organization can invite guest users including admins (most restrictive)

options.text: Select 'Anyone in the organization can invite guest users including guests and non-admins (most inclusive)'
Select 'Member users and users assigned to specific admin roles can invite guest users including guests with member permissions'
Select 'Only users assigned to specific admin roles can invite guest users'
Select 'No one in the organization can invite guest users including admins (most restrictive)'

explanation.correct: The radio button 'Only users assigned to specific admin roles can invite guest users' lets you restrict invitations to people who hold designated admin roles, which by default includes the Guest Inviter and User Administrator roles. Users with the Guest Inviter role can still issue invitations when this option is selected.

perChoice.A: This is the most inclusive option, which permits every user and every existing guest to invite others and does not satisfy the requirement.
perChoice.B: This option still allows all member users to invite guests, so it does not restrict invitations to admin roles only.
perChoice.D: This option blocks every user including administrators, which is more restrictive than the requirement and would prevent the Guest Inviter role from working.

body.stem: You administer a Microsoft Entra workforce tenant at fabrikam.onmicrosoft.com. You invited the partner contact john@contoso.com to the directory using the Microsoft Entra admin center, and the partner has redeemed the invitation. You need to identify the User Principal Name (UPN) value that Microsoft Entra ID assigns to the resulting guest user object. Which value should you expect?

options.text: john@contoso.com#EXT#@fabrikam.onmicrosoft.com
john_contoso.com#EXT#@fabrikam.onmicrosoft.com
john_contoso.com@fabrikam.onmicrosoft.com#EXT#
john.contoso.com#EXT#@fabrikam.onmicrosoft.com

explanation.correct: Microsoft Entra ID records B2B guest user UPNs in the format emailaddress#EXT#@resource-tenant-domain, where the at-sign in the original email is replaced with an underscore. For john@contoso.com invited into fabrikam.onmicrosoft.com, the resulting UPN is john_contoso.com#EXT#@fabrikam.onmicrosoft.com.

perChoice.A: Leaves the original at-sign from john@contoso.com inside the local part. Microsoft Entra replaces the @ with an underscore before appending the #EXT# identifier and the resource tenant domain.
perChoice.C: Places the #EXT# identifier after the resource tenant domain. The convention puts #EXT# between the email-derived local part and the resource domain, not at the very end of the UPN.
perChoice.D: Replaces the @ in the original email with a period instead of an underscore. Only the underscore substitution is supported, so this format will not match what Microsoft Entra ID assigns.

body.stem: You administer a Microsoft Entra workforce tenant at fabrikam.onmicrosoft.com. A partner user from partner.com has redeemed a B2B invitation and now signs in to your shared SalesApp enterprise application. Your security team asks which tenants record an authentication event for this sign-in. Which combination of tenants logs the B2B sign-in?

options.text: Only your resource tenant (fabrikam.onmicrosoft.com) logs the sign-in
Only the partner home tenant (partner.com) logs the sign-in
Both the partner home tenant and your resource tenant log the sign-in
Neither tenant logs the sign-in; records flow only to a separate audit pipeline that does not involve the tenants

explanation.correct: When a B2B user signs in to a resource tenant to collaborate, Microsoft Entra ID creates a sign-in log in both the partner home tenant and your resource tenant. Each log captures the application used, email addresses, tenant name, and tenant ID for both the home and resource tenant so either side can investigate the activity.

perChoice.A: The resource tenant does record the event, but the partner home tenant also records it. Limiting logging to the resource tenant alone misses the half of the audit trail held by the guest's home directory.
perChoice.B: The partner home tenant does record the event, but the resource tenant records it as well. Restricting logs to the home tenant alone loses the event from the tenant that actually authorized access to your application.
perChoice.D: Microsoft Entra ID writes the B2B sign-in events into the two participating tenants themselves. There is no separate, tenant-independent pipeline that receives B2B sign-in records in place of those tenant logs.

body.stem: You administer a Microsoft Entra tenant for a federal agency that is hosted in Microsoft Azure Government. The agency needs to enable B2B collaboration so that vendors whose organizations use Microsoft Entra tenants in the Azure global cloud can be invited as guest users to a shared line-of-business application. You need to set up B2B collaboration between tenants that are running in different Microsoft Azure clouds. Which task must be completed first?

options.text: Configure Microsoft cloud settings in both tenants to enable collaboration with the other cloud.
Add each partner's verified domain to the allow list in the resource tenant's external collaboration settings.
Configure B2B direct connect between the agency's tenant and each partner tenant.
Migrate the agency's tenant from Microsoft Azure Government to the Azure global cloud.

explanation.correct: Establishing B2B collaboration between tenants in different Microsoft Azure clouds (such as Azure Government and the global cloud) requires each tenant to configure its Microsoft cloud settings to enable collaboration with the other cloud, after which each tenant configures inbound and outbound cross-tenant access. This is the documented first step for cross-cloud B2B.

perChoice.b: Adding domains to the allow list in external collaboration settings controls per-domain invitation policy within a single cloud; it does not establish the mutual cross-cloud relationship required between Azure Government and the global cloud.
perChoice.c: B2B direct connect is intended for sharing Microsoft Teams channels between tenants and is not the mechanism used to enable cross-cloud B2B collaboration between Azure Government and the global cloud.
perChoice.d: Migrating a tenant out of Azure Government is not a supported or practical step and is not required to enable B2B collaboration with partners in another Microsoft cloud.

body.stem: You administer a Microsoft Entra workforce tenant at fabrikam.onmicrosoft.com. A user administrator previously invited an external partner, alex@partner.com, to the directory using the New user > Invite external user option in the Microsoft Entra admin center. Two days later, Alex reports never receiving the invitation email. The invited user object already exists in your directory, but the partner has not redeemed the invitation. You need to give Alex a working invitation link without deleting and recreating the directory object. Which action should you perform?

options.text: From the user object, open the B2B collaboration tile under My Feed and select Resend invitation to send a new invitation email.
Delete the user object, then use New user > Invite external user and re-enter Alex's email address to recreate the account.
Change the user's User type from Guest to Member, save, then change it back to Guest and save again.
Add Alex to a new security group and wait for synchronization to propagate a fresh invitation link.

explanation.correct: When a B2B-collaboration invitation email is lost or never delivered, the Microsoft Entra admin center lets an administrator issue another email directly from the invited user's properties. As described in 'Add and manage B2B collaboration users in the Microsoft Entra admin center', on the user's page, in the My Feed section, the B2B collaboration tile exposes a Resend invitation link when the Invitation state shows Pending acceptance.

perChoice.b: Deleting and recreating the user object is unnecessary when the existing object's invitation can simply be re-sent, and it would also drop any group or role assignments already associated with that guest.
perChoice.c: Toggling the User type between Guest and Member changes directory classification only; it does not generate a new invitation email and does not address a missed email.
perChoice.d: Adding the user to a group changes entitlements but does not produce a new invitation email for an unredeemed partner.

body.stem: You administer a Microsoft Entra workforce tenant at fabrikam.onmicrosoft.com. Your security team directs that any external guest user must satisfy MFA when accessing the SalesHub enterprise application. MFA prompts must NOT be introduced for internal member users on any application, and MFA prompts must NOT be introduced for guests on any application other than SalesHub. You need to apply this requirement using Microsoft Entra Conditional Access without changing the tenant-wide default behavior. Which policy action should you take?

exhibit.text:
Fabrikam Conditional Access policies

Policy name           | State | Assignments                  | Cloud apps     | Controls
Tenant-MFA-All        | Off   | All users                    | All cloud apps | Require MFA
SalesHub-Block-Strict | Off   | All users                    | SalesHub       | Block access
Guests-All-Apps-MFA   | Off   | All guest or external users  | All cloud apps | Require MFA

options.text: Create a new policy that targets All guest or external users, includes SalesHub in its cloud apps, and uses Require MFA as its grant control; then enable the policy.
Enable the Guests-All-Apps-MFA policy because it already targets All guest or external users with Require MFA.
Enable the SalesHub-Block-Strict policy because blocking access is a stronger control than MFA on SalesHub.
Modify the Tenant-MFA-All policy by removing SalesHub from its cloud apps scope, then enable it so the remaining apps still require MFA.

explanation.correct: Per 'What is Microsoft Entra B2B collaboration?', Conditional Access policies (such as MFA) can be enforced at the tenant level, at the application level, or for specific guest users. The only way to require MFA only for guests on SalesHub is to create a new Conditional Access policy that targets All guest or external users, includes only SalesHub under cloud apps, and uses Require MFA as its grant control, then enable it.

perChoice.b: Enabling the Guests-All-Apps-MFA policy would require MFA for guests on every cloud app, not only SalesHub, which violates the constraint that no MFA prompt may be introduced for guests on applications other than SalesHub.
perChoice.c: Blocking access is not the same as enforcing MFA; the SalesHub-Block-Strict policy would deny access rather than require MFA, and the requirement is MFA specifically, not access denial.
perChoice.d: Modifying Tenant-MFA-All by removing SalesHub only leaves MFA in place for everyone on the other apps, which does not introduce MFA for guests on SalesHub and also affects internal members on other apps, violating both constraints.

body.stem: You administer a Microsoft Entra workforce tenant. The current External Identities > External collaboration settings are shown in the exhibit. Your compliance team now requires that every new external sign-up must pass through your existing custom approval workflow before a user object is created in your directory. You need the sign-up process to invoke this workflow automatically for each registration, before the user is committed. Which capability should you add?

exhibit.text:
Property                                         | Value
Guest user access                                | Guests have limited access (default level)
Guest invite settings                            | Anyone in the organization can invite guests
Enable guest self-service sign up via user flows | Yes
External user leave settings                     | No
Collaboration restrictions                       | None

options.text: An API connector added as an inline step during the sign-up experience
A conditional access policy enforcing MFA before each sign-up completes
A dynamic-membership group that automatically contains every newly signed-up user
An access review performed on each newly created guest account, run by your compliance team

explanation.correct: API connectors can be added as inline steps inside a self-service sign-up user flow, allowing the sign-up process to call an external HTTP-based service such as a custom approval workflow before the user object is created in the directory.

perChoice.b: A conditional access policy is enforced at sign-in time for existing users and applications; it cannot be inserted as an inline step inside a self-service sign-up user flow.
perChoice.c: A dynamic-membership group adds or removes users based on attribute evaluation, but membership is only evaluated after the user object already exists in the directory; it cannot intercept the sign-up to invoke an approval workflow before user creation.
perChoice.d: An access review is a governance activity that periodically checks existing assignments; it cannot be invoked inline during sign-up to gate user object creation behind an approval workflow.

body.stem: You administer a Microsoft Entra workforce tenant. The owners of several enterprise apps, none of whom hold administrator responsibilities, must be able to add partner collaborators to the apps they own from their own portal page, instead of a central administrator adding each guest account on their behalf. Which capability should you configure?

rows: Owners have no option to add users; a central administrator adds every guest account
Partner users signing up for an app
Turned on through a sign-up user flow
Recurring certification of existing app and group assignments

options.text: Self-service app and group management
Self-service sign-up user flows
Access reviews for app and group assignments
Dynamic membership for apps and groups

explanation.correct: Microsoft Entra lets you delegate guest onboarding to application and group owners. An administrator turns on self-service app and group management, and afterwards non-administrator owners add guest users to applications or groups themselves from their own portal page, rather than an administrator adding every account individually. That matches the requirement stated here and the tenant's current gap (owners have no option to add users today).

perChoice.b: Sign-up user flows are for end users registering themselves for an app, where a new guest account is created as part of that registration. They do not hand the ability to add partner guests to app owners, and this tenant already has a sign-up user flow in place.
perChoice.c: Access reviews are used to periodically certify, and where necessary remove, access that people already hold. They do not provide a way for an owner to bring a new partner guest into an app.
perChoice.d: Dynamic membership builds group membership automatically from user attributes that match a rule. It gives owners no way to add a partner guest to an application, and this tenant already has dynamic groups configured.

body.stem: You administer a Microsoft Entra workforce tenant. You need to know which Entra admin area to configure for different B2B-related outcomes. Match each outcome to the admin area that produces it.

items.text: Allowing or blocking invitations to a specific external partner domain
Determining whether external Microsoft Entra users may sign in to your resources
Establishing mutual collaboration between an Azure global tenant and an Azure Government tenant
Defining Conditional Access policy assignments for guest access to specific apps

explanation.correct: Allow-or-block domains is governed by External collaboration settings. Whether external Microsoft Entra users can authenticate into your resources is governed by Cross-tenant access settings. Enabling collaboration between tenants in different Microsoft Azure clouds is governed by Microsoft cloud settings.

perChoice.a: Maps to External collaboration settings: the documentation lists Allow or block domains as one of the options configured under External Identities > External collaboration settings.
perChoice.b: Maps to Cross-tenant access settings: the documentation states this area controls whether users can authenticate with external Microsoft Entra tenants and applies to inbound and outbound B2B collaboration.
perChoice.c: Maps to Microsoft cloud settings: the documentation states this area establishes mutual B2B collaboration between tenants in different Microsoft Azure clouds such as global and Government.
perChoice.d: Fits no slot: Conditional Access policy assignments are configured under Entra ID > Security > Conditional Access, not under any of the three External Identities settings areas shown.

body.stem: You administer a Microsoft Entra workforce tenant. In External Identities > External collaboration settings, the Guest user access section offers three radio-button levels. You need to understand what each level grants. Match each description to the radio-button level that produces it.

items.text: Guests have the same access to directory data and resources as member users
Guests are blocked from enumerating users and groups but can view the membership of any non-hidden group
Guests can only access the properties and memberships of their own user object
Guests can view every user's full profile but cannot view group memberships

explanation.correct: The Guest user access section provides three radio-button levels. Most inclusive matches the option Guest users have the same access as members. Default matches the option that limits access to properties and memberships but still lets guests see non-hidden group memberships. Most restrictive matches the option that limits guests to only their own directory objects.

perChoice.a: Maps to Most inclusive: the documentation describes this level as Guest users have the same access as members (most inclusive).
perChoice.b: Maps to Default: the documentation describes this level as Guest users have limited access to properties and memberships of directory objects, where guests can see membership of all non-hidden groups.
perChoice.c: Maps to Most restrictive: the documentation describes this level as Guest user access is restricted to properties and memberships of their own directory objects (most restrictive).
perChoice.d: Fits no slot: this combination is not one of the three radio-button options listed under Guest user access in the documentation.

body.stem: You administer a Microsoft Entra workforce tenant. In External Identities > External collaboration settings, the Guest invite settings section offers four radio-button options. You need to understand what each option permits. Match each description to the radio-button label that produces it.

items.text: All users in the organization, including guests and non-admins, can issue invitations
Member users and admin role holders can invite, along with guests having member-level permissions
Just accounts holding the User Administrator or Guest Inviter roles can send invitations
Nobody in the organization, including admins, can issue invitations

explanation.correct: The Guest invite settings section provides four radio-button options. Most inclusive matches Anyone in the organization. Internal users plus admin roles matches the option for Member users and admin role holders that also lets external users with member-level permissions invite. Admin roles only matches the option for User Administrator or Guest Inviter role holders. Most restrictive matches the option for nobody including admins.

perChoice.a: Maps to Most inclusive: the documentation describes this level as Anyone in the organization can invite guest users including guests and non-admins (most inclusive).
perChoice.b: Maps to Internal users plus admin roles: the documentation describes this level as Member users and users assigned to specific admin roles can invite guest users including guests with member permissions.
perChoice.c: Maps to Admin roles only: the documentation describes this level as Only users assigned to specific admin roles can invite guest users, explicitly naming User Administrator or Guest Inviter roles.
perChoice.d: Maps to Most restrictive: the documentation describes this level as No one in the organization can invite guest users including admins (most restrictive).

body.stem: You administer a Microsoft Entra workforce tenant. You need to delegate B2B invitation rights using the least-privileged directory role for each scenario, without granting unnecessary account-management powers. Match each requirement to the directory role that satisfies it.

items.text: Invite external users when the 'Only users assigned to specific administrator roles can invite guest users' option is selected, without granting account-management rights
Assign a Microsoft Entra directory role to an external guest at the time of invitation
Serve as the minimum sign-in role for performing the full external user invite workflow in the admin center
Create a new internal account with the user type set to Member

explanation.correct: Guest Inviter allows inviting guests without granting account-management powers and works when the admin-roles-only invite option is selected. Privileged Role Administrator is the role required specifically when assigning Microsoft Entra directory roles to a new guest during invitation. User Administrator is the minimum role for performing the full external user invite workflow in the admin center.

perChoice.a: Maps to Guest Inviter: the documentation states that with this role, users can invite guests even when Only users assigned to specific admin roles can invite guest users is selected, and notes it does not grant higher-privilege administrator powers.
perChoice.b: Maps to Privileged Role Administrator: the documentation states The Privileged Role Administrator role is required to assign Microsoft Entra roles during the external user invite workflow.
perChoice.c: Maps to User Administrator: the documentation states you must sign in to the Microsoft Entra admin center as at least a User Administrator to invite external users and assign them to groups at the same time.
perChoice.d: Fits no slot: creating a brand-new member account is not part of the B2B external user invite workflow described in the documentation.

body.stem: You administer a Microsoft Entra workforce tenant at fabrikam.onmicrosoft.com. A user administrator has just invited an external partner, john@contoso.com, by using Microsoft Entra ID > Users > New user > Invite external user. Before the partner has redeemed the invitation, you open the new user object. The exhibit lists some of the properties observed on that object. You need to match each B2B-specific property to the value Microsoft Entra ID assigns to it for an external invitee.

exhibit.text:
Property               | Value
-----------------------|------------------------------------------------
Display name           | John Smith
Mail                   | john@contoso.com
Source                 | External Azure Active Directory
Job title              | Partner Consultant

items.text: Guest
Member
Pending acceptance
john_contoso.com#EXT#@fabrikam.onmicrosoft.com
Accepted

explanation.correct: For an external invitee, Microsoft Entra ID stores User type as Guest, formats the User principal name as emailaddress#EXT#@inviting_domain, and records Invitation state as Pending acceptance until the partner redeems the invitation.

perChoice.a: Maps to User type: the documentation states the invited user's account is added to Microsoft Entra ID with a user type of Guest.
perChoice.b: Not a match: Member is the user type used for accounts that belong to your organization, not for external invitees added through Invite external user.
perChoice.c: Maps to Invitation state: the documentation shows the invitation state remains Pending acceptance until the invitee redeems the invitation via the email link.
perChoice.d: Maps to User principal name: the documentation shows the format emailaddress#EXT#@domain, with the example john_contoso.com#EXT#@fabrikam.onmicrosoft.com.
perChoice.e: Not a match: Accepted reflects the state after the invitee redeems the invitation, not the state at the moment the invite is first sent.

body.stem: You administer a Microsoft Entra workforce tenant. Four teams have handed you external partner onboarding tasks, each of which is completed at a different starting point in the Microsoft Entra admin center. Drag each item to the navigation path you should open to complete that task.

items.text: Invite a contact from outside the organization as a B2B guest in the directory so they can later be assigned to apps and groups.
Place an existing external partner into a security group so they inherit the permissions assigned to the group.
Grant one external partner direct access to a single application in the tenant.
Allow external people to register themselves for an application using their existing credentials, without any administrator invitation.

slots.label: Microsoft Entra ID > Users > New user > Invite external user
Microsoft Entra ID > Groups > [Group] > Members > Add members
Microsoft Entra ID > Enterprise apps > [App] > Users and groups > Add user/group
External Identities > External collaboration settings > Enable guest self-service sign up via user flows

explanation.correct: Each scenario is handled at a different starting point: inviting a new B2B guest is done from the Users node under Microsoft Entra ID, adding an existing partner to a security group is done from that group's Members node, granting a single partner direct access to one application is done from that app's Users and groups node, and allowing external people to register themselves is enabled under External Identities > External collaboration settings.

perChoice.i1: A new B2B guest who is not yet represented in the directory is created by selecting New user > Invite external user under Microsoft Entra ID > Users.
perChoice.i2: An existing directory partner is added to a security group by opening the group under Microsoft Entra ID > Groups and selecting Add members under its Members node.
perChoice.i3: Direct access for a single external partner to a single enterprise application is granted by opening the application under Microsoft Entra ID > Enterprise apps and selecting Add user/group under its Users and groups node.
perChoice.i4: Allowing external people to sign up themselves without an admin invitation is enabled by turning on 'Enable guest self-service sign up via user flows' under External Identities > External collaboration settings, after which a self-service sign-up user flow can be built and attached to an app.

body.stem: You administer a Microsoft Entra workforce tenant. A user administrator is using the New user wizard in Microsoft Entra ID > Users to create a new B2B collaboration guest. The administrator wants to add the new guest to as many existing security groups as possible within the single + Add group step. You need to know the maximum number of groups that can be selected there in one pass.
body.statement: Within the + Add group step of the New user > Invite external user wizard, the maximum number of groups that can be selected in one pass is {{count}}.

explanation.correct: Per the documentation, within the + Add group step of the New user > Invite external user wizard, the menu lets the administrator choose up to 20 groups in a single pass; further group memberships are added through subsequent assignments.

perChoice.count:a: 5 is below the documented per-step cap of 20.
perChoice.count:b: 10 is below the documented per-step cap of 20.
perChoice.count:d: 50 exceeds the documented per-step cap of 20.

body.stem: You administer a Microsoft Entra workforce tenant. A user administrator enters distribution-group@partner.com, a shared contact at the partner's company, into the wizard, intending that several partner colleagues all redeem the same link. You need to determine how Microsoft Entra processes this address.
body.statement: When the address distribution-group@partner.com is entered in the wizard as the contact, Microsoft Entra {{result}}.

options.text: Microsoft Entra shares the invitation; every member of the contact list redeems the same guest account
Microsoft Entra doesn't accept group addresses here; each individual mailbox must be invited separately
Microsoft Entra rejects the entry unless External collaboration settings is changed to allow group addresses
Microsoft Entra accepts the contact and routes it to B2B direct connect rather than standard B2B collaboration

explanation.correct: The documentation states explicitly that group email addresses are not supported in the Email field of the invitation wizard; the entry must be an individual email address, and each individual mailbox must be sent its own invitation.

perChoice.result:a: The wizard does not create a shared guest account that every member of a group-style address redeems; group email addresses are not supported as the Email input.
perChoice.result:c: External collaboration settings govern which roles and domains may send invitations; they do not control whether the Email field accepts group-style addresses.
perChoice.result:d: B2B direct connect is intended for shared resources such as Teams channels, not as a routing alternative for group-style addresses in the invitation wizard.

body.stem: You administer a Microsoft Entra workforce tenant. You want partner users without an existing Microsoft Entra ID account to redeem a B2B invitation by signing in through their personal Google or Facebook account, rather than registering a Microsoft-branded account for the redeeming step. You need to identify which Microsoft Entra capability lets your tenant accept sign-ins from these consumer accounts.
body.statement: The Microsoft Entra capability that lets your tenant accept B2B sign-ins from consumer credentials such as Google or Facebook is called {{capability}}.

options.text: Federation with external identity providers
Cross-tenant access settings
Self-service sign-up user flows
External collaboration settings

explanation.correct: The documentation states that Microsoft Entra External ID supports external identity providers such as Facebook, Google, and enterprise identity providers, and that setting up federation with those providers lets guests sign in with their existing social or enterprise accounts rather than registering a new one.

perChoice.capability:b: Cross-tenant access settings govern inbound and outbound B2B with other Microsoft Entra organizations; they do not enable sign-in from consumer account providers such as Google or Facebook.
perChoice.capability:c: Self-service sign-up user flows is a sign-up experience that can be built on top of identity providers; the underlying capability that lets the tenant accept Google or Facebook credentials is federation with those external identity providers.
perChoice.capability:d: External collaboration settings control who in your organization may send invitations and which domains are allowed or blocked; they do not by themselves accept consumer account provider sign-ins.

body.stem: You administer a Microsoft Entra workforce tenant. A partner requests an invitation, providing their address as jane+project@partner.com. The email pattern is commonly used by the partner's mail provider for inbox filtering. You need to identify the recommended action when issuing the B2B invitation.
body.statement: When the address jane+project@partner.com is supplied, the recommended action before sending the invitation is to {{action}}.

options.text: Omit the plus character and any characters following it up to the @ symbol
Send the invitation unchanged because plus-aliasing is universally supported
Replace the @ with #EXT#@ so the invitation is delivered to the partner's home tenant
Reformat the address as jane_partner.com#EXT# so it matches the expected UPN format

explanation.correct: The documentation states that Microsoft Entra does not currently support plus symbols in email addresses, and that to avoid delivery issues the plus character and any characters following it up to the @ symbol must be omitted from the address.

perChoice.action:b: Plus symbols are not supported in Microsoft Entra email addresses; the address must be adjusted before the invitation is sent.
perChoice.action:c: Replacing the @ symbol with #EXT#@ is not how invitation delivery works; the local-part needs to be sanitized to drop the plus and everything between it and the @.
perChoice.action:d: Reformatting the address into a #EXT# style value is not the supported sanitization; the documented guidance is to drop the plus character and the characters that follow it up to the @.

body.stem: You administer a workforce directory tenant. Your development team needs to programmatically add external partners, customize the redemption experience, and integrate with custom approval workflows beyond the standard wizard in the admin center. You need to identify the API surface for these partner onboarding scenarios.
body.statement: The API surface made available for developers to programmatically add external partners and customize the redemption experience is called {{surface}}.

options.text: Microsoft Entra business-to-business APIs
Microsoft Graph user APIs
Azure subscription management APIs
Microsoft 365 admin center automation APIs

explanation.correct: The documentation states that developers use Microsoft Entra business-to-business APIs to customize the invitation process and write applications such as self-service sign-up portals; the B2B collaboration invitation APIs are the dedicated surface for these partner onboarding scenarios.

perChoice.surface:b: Microsoft Graph user APIs are a broader general-purpose identity surface; the documentation calls out Microsoft Entra business-to-business APIs as the specific surface for customizing B2B invitation and redemption flows.
perChoice.surface:c: Azure subscription management APIs (Azure Resource Manager) cover subscription and resource lifecycle operations; they are not the surface for customizing guest invitation redemption.
perChoice.surface:d: Microsoft 365 admin center automation APIs serve tenant-level Microsoft 365 service administration and are not documented as the surface for customizing B2B partner onboarding.

body.stem: You administer a Microsoft Entra workforce tenant for Fabrikam, and you want to change tenant-wide B2B settings through Microsoft Graph automation rather than clicking through the admin center. Your compliance team has asked you to change the two settings shown in the exhibit, and you need to know which single Microsoft Graph resource type stores the values behind both of them. Which resource type should your automation target?

rows: Guest users have limited access to properties and memberships of directory objects
Anyone in the organization can invite guest users including guests and non-admins

body.statement: Your automation should target the Microsoft Graph {{graphResource}} resource type, because that is the resource that stores the values for both of the settings shown in the exhibit.

options.text: authorizationPolicy
authenticationFlowsPolicy
externalidentitiespolicy
emailAuthenticationMethodConfiguration

explanation.correct: The Microsoft Graph documentation for configuring external collaboration settings states that the guest user access restrictions and the guest invite restrictions are both stored in the authorizationPolicy resource type, so the keyed option is the single resource an automation run would patch to change both values in the exhibit.

perChoice.graphResource:b: authenticationFlowsPolicy is the resource that holds the setting for enabling guest self-service sign-up through user flows, not the directory-visibility level or the invitation permissions shown in the exhibit.
perChoice.graphResource:c: externalidentitiespolicy is the resource that holds the external user leave settings, which control whether external users can remove themselves from the organization; it does not hold guest visibility or invitation restrictions.
perChoice.graphResource:d: emailAuthenticationMethodConfiguration is the resource that holds the email one-time passcode settings, which govern how a guest authenticates; it is unrelated to who may invite guests or what guests can see in the directory.
